cases.question: What do exact and approximate results mean in this graph library?

response.message: Exact means the declared mathematical result is established when execution completes. A heuristic does not guarantee an optimum. Numerical results have their declared tolerances; stochastic and learned results have different guarantees. Complete output means no requested result rows were omitted; it does not make a heuristic exact. Check each operation's quality and solution_quality contract.

cases.question: Explain maximal versus maximum cliques without running an analysis.

response.message: Every pair of vertices in a clique is connected. A maximal clique cannot be extended by adding another vertex. A maximum clique has the largest size of any clique in the graph. All maximum cliques are maximal, but maximal cliques can be smaller than the maximum.

trace.message: A clique is a set of vertices where every pair is connected. A **maximal** clique is one that cannot be extended by adding another vertex while preserving the all-pairs-connected property. A **maximum** clique is the largest such set in the entire graph. Every maximum clique is necessarily maximal, but a maximal clique need not be the largest—there can be many maximal cliques of different sizes, and only the biggest one(s) are maximum. {{doc.clique-terms}}

measurement_notes: One attempt per question, including product retries and answer composition; fixture setup is timed separately.
Real current lanes are recorded without translating calculation into lookup or options.
Selected-card request fields are sent unchanged; an unsupported request contract counts as a failure.
Data answers require structured evidence; prose semantics and general explanation quality are not human-reviewed.
Phase 5 grounding separately verifies final answer text against tool-evidence events from the same turn, without trusting checked flags.
No production writes, training captures, or persistent development configuration changes.
Observed timings include local server/cache conditions and are not controlled performance benchmarks.
